statement: In the primary clinical discovery cohort of 8 unrelated individuals with de novo putative loss-of-function variants in TAF4 (Janssen et al., 2022), global developmental delay / intellectual disability (HP:0001263 / HP:0001249) and disproportionate expressive language delay (HP:0000750) both occurred in 8/8 (100%) patients.
caveat: Ascertained from a small discovery cohort of n=8 individuals carrying de novo pLoF variants; missense variants in sporadic developmental language disorder cohorts (Kennis et al., 2026) can present with isolated expressive speech impairment and preserved non-verbal IQ >= 70.

statement: In the Janssen et al. (2022) cohort of 8 individuals with de novo pLoF variants in TAF4, behavioral abnormalities (HP:0000708) and category-level facial dysmorphisms (HP:0001999) were each documented in 7/8 (87.5%) patients.
caveat: Although category-level facial dysmorphism is penetrant (7/8, 87.5%), individual morphological features are highly variable and none is pathognomonic across all patients.
report_quote: | Behavioral abnormalities (hyperactivity, impulsivity, autism traits) | Abnormality of behavior (HP:0000708) | Primary clinical cohort (Janssen et al., 2022, DOI: 10.1002/humu.24444) | 7/8 | 87.5% | F6 |

statement: In the primary clinical cohort of Janssen et al. (2022), discrete facial anomalies such as arched eyebrows (HP:0002553), epicanthus (HP:0000286), and thin upper lip vermilion (HP:0000219) each occurred in fewer than 6/8 (<75%) patients.
caveat: No single discrete facial feature exceeds 75% penetrance (<6/8), preventing definitive phenotypic diagnosis based on physical exam alone.
